providers.name: Provider name
providers.get_key_title: Go to the provider's website to get an API key
providers.history_reasoning_desc: Newer models (e.g. DeepSeek V4) require reasoning_content to be echoed back. When enabled, the reasoning_content of past assistant messages is sent with each request; models that don't need it ignore the field silently. Turn this off if a provider rejects requests over the unrecognized field.
providers.prompt_cache_desc: When enabled, adds cache_control to the system prompt and the second-to-last user message to reuse Anthropic's prompt cache.
providers.prompt_cache_key_desc: Attach a per-conversation prompt_cache_key so official OpenAI endpoints can route requests of the same conversation to the same cache shard, improving cache hits. Some third-party endpoints may reject this field; enable as needed.
providers.interactions_desc: Route chat requests through Google's Interactions endpoint (next-generation protocol with thinking summaries, signed function calls, and image output). When off, the standard generateContent endpoint is used; only the official Gemini endpoint supports it.
providers.custom_headers_desc: Attached to every request of this provider (chat, model list, balance lookup, etc.). When the same header is also set at the assistant or model level, this provider-level value has the lowest priority.
providers.prompt_cache_warming_desc_official: Sessions resend a request shortly before the cache expires to renew it and save cost.
providers.prompt_cache_warming_desc_other: If the upstream provider keeps Anthropic's cache, workspace sessions resend a request shortly before the cache expires to renew it and save cost.
providers.models_desc: Fetch the provider's models first, then check the ones to enable. {{count}} currently enabled.

providers.no_models: No models yet. Click “Add model” to add one manually, or “Fetch models” to sync from upstream.

providers.reasoning_enabled: Reasoning is enabled — click to disable

assistants.name: Assistant name
assistants.system_prompt_cache_hint: Note: the cur_time / cur_datetime / time variables are second-precision and change on every request, which prevents prompt cache hits. Prefer the day-level cur_date unless needed.

assistants.delete_confirm_with_memories: Delete the assistant "{{name}}"? It has {{n}} memories.
assistants.message_template_desc: Wraps the user message before sending it to the model. Usually fine to leave as default.

assistants.preview_assistant_response: Hello, how can I help you?
assistants.preset_messages_desc: These preset messages are written when a new conversation is created, giving the assistant a stable opening context.
assistants.regex_desc: Runs substitutions after user input or assistant output; invalid regexes are skipped automatically.
assistants.param_default_desc: Not set: the parameter is omitted and the model default applies. Drag or type a value to set it.
assistants.max_tokens_desc: Leave empty to omit it and use the server default.

assistants.local_tools_desc: Local tool list. When enabled, they're injected only if the current model supports tool calls.

time_info.title: Time info

ask_user.title: Ask user

assistants.bodies_desc: Merged into the request body by key; the value can be JSON or a plain string.

proxy.ua_desc: Customize the User-Agent header sent with outbound requests. Leave blank to use the default. Only change this if your provider (e.g. a corporate gateway or API relay) requires a specific User-Agent.
proxy.none_detected_desc: The system proxy is off, or the proxy tool hasn't started yet.
proxy.pac_detected_desc: This app does not support PAC scripts. Check your proxy tool for its HTTP proxy port and fill in the address manually (e.g. 127.0.0.1:7890).
proxy.port_desc: Port the local service listens on, default {{port}}. Leave blank to auto-select; a fixed port is used when set, walking up if occupied. Takes effect after restart.
proxy.port_invalid: Port must be an integer between 1 and 65535
proxy.port_restart_note: Port changes take effect after restarting. The running instance still uses the old port.
proxy.port_container_locked: In container deployments the port is decided by the image and docker -p mapping; changing it here has no effect.
proxy.restart_failed: Restart failed. Please quit and reopen the app manually.
proxy.socks_not_supported: SOCKS proxy is not supported (runtime limitation). Please use the proxy tool's HTTP port.
proxy.mode_auto_desc: Automatically follow the system proxy (Windows registry / GNOME settings).
proxy.mode_manual_desc: Use the fixed HTTP proxy specified below.
proxy.mode_direct_desc: Ignore the system proxy entirely; all requests go direct (an escape hatch when the system proxy is broken).
proxy.mode_env_desc: Controlled by HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY environment variables (common in container deployments).
proxy.env_desktop_hint: In the desktop app, please use Manual mode — Env mode only applies to Docker deployments; the desktop app clears proxy environment variables at startup, so this mode always connects directly.
proxy.container_mode_desc: Container deployment: the proxy is controlled by docker environment variables (HTTPS_PROXY, etc.) and cannot be changed here. Configure it in docker-compose or docker run.
proxy.bypass_rules_desc: Matching hosts connect directly without the proxy (localhost / 127.0.0.1 always bypass). Comma-separated; *.example.com wildcards and 10.0.0.0/8 CIDR ranges supported.
proxy.url_invalid: Invalid proxy URL. Expected http(s)://host:port or host:port.

chat.title: Primary model
chat.desc: The main model for conversations and work tasks. Used when no model is manually selected on the home page.

optimize.title: Prompt optimization
optimize.desc: The model used by the “Optimize prompt” button. It rewrites your draft more clearly and professionally based on context. When unset, it follows the current conversation's primary model.

fast.title: Fast model
fast.desc: A lightweight model for generating conversation titles and chat suggestions

translate.title: Translation
translate.desc: The model used for translation. When unset, it follows the current conversation's primary model.

compress.title: Context compression
compress.desc: The model for compressing long conversations, keeping key context and writing it back to the conversation. When unset, it follows the current conversation's primary model.

ocr.title: OCR
ocr.desc: A fallback image-to-text channel for chat models without vision input. When unset, this channel is unavailable.

image.title: Image generation
image.desc: Entry point for models with image generation capability. Image generation is unavailable until a model is set.

speech.step_instruction_desc: Omitted when empty; step-tts-mini / vivid ignore this field.

guide.title: How plugins work
guide.intro: Plugins are extension packages written for the pi engine. They add tools, commands and automated behaviors to workspace conversations. This page explains how they run in the app, which parts don't take effect, and where to look when something goes wrong.

trust.title: First: plugins are code running on your computer
trust.code: A plugin has the same permissions as the app: it can read and write your files, use the network, start other programs, and read the key of the model the conversation uses. The app doesn't check what plugins do and can't guarantee they work as described.
trust.process: Plugins run in a separate engine process, so one that hangs or crashes won't take the whole app down. That process is not a sandbox and won't stop a malicious plugin.
trust.sources: Only install from sources you trust, and look at a plugin's homepage and description before installing it.

use.title: Using plugins
use.enable: After installing, turn a plugin on for the current conversation in "$t(input:integrations.title)" → "$t(settings:subnav.extensions.plugins)" at the bottom left of the input box. To turn it on by default for an assistant's new conversations, go to "Settings → $t(settings:nav.assistants) → $t(settings:assistants.extensions.title)".
use.workspace_only: Plugins only load in workspace conversations. They have no effect in chat mode.
use.changes: Turning a plugin on or off for a conversation, disabling or uninstalling it, and changing its tool switches all take effect from the next message. A reply in progress isn't affected.

overlap.title: What doesn't take effect
overlap.app_owned: Parts the app handles itself don't take effect even if a plugin registers them: models and sign-in (adding providers, switching models, changing the thinking level), rewriting requests sent to the model, creating, forking or switching conversations, entry commands (/settings, /model, /new, /fork and so on; the app's own versions apply), and permission prompts before tool calls (see "Approval" below).
overlap.mcp: MCP servers declared by a plugin don't run inside the plugin. They are added to "Settings → $t(settings:nav.extensions) → $t(settings:subnav.extensions.mcp)" and marked as from the plugin. They follow the plugin when it's enabled or disabled, and you can also turn them off on the MCP page.
overlap.terminal: Parts that need a terminal interface aren't supported: themes, keyboard shortcuts, custom terminal components and message renderers.
overlap.background: Background sub-tasks aren't supported: a task the plugin runs by starting a separate command-line process fails right away. Sub-tasks that run inside the current conversation work.
overlap.resources: Skills, prompt templates and themes bundled in a plugin package aren't loaded. Manage skills in "Settings → $t(settings:nav.extensions) → $t(settings:subnav.extensions.skills)".
overlap.same_name: A plugin tool with the same name as one of the app's tools isn't loaded (including the workspace tools that read and write files and run commands).
overlap.where: The top of a plugin's detail page says how many features didn't take effect. Click "$t(settings:plugins.view)" to open "$t(settings:plugins.tab_audit)", which lists each part that didn't take effect and why. Activity appears only after the plugin has loaded with a conversation, and only covers the time since the app last started.

search.title: Web search plugins
search.coexist: Search and web-fetch tools from plugins are available alongside the app's own web search, and the model picks which to use. Plugin tools ask for approval by the rules under "Approval" below, and their results show as ordinary tool cards.
search.turn_off: To use only one side: to turn off the app's, click the search button at the bottom left of the input box and switch off "$t(input:search.web_title)" in the "$t(input:search.title)" panel that opens (applies to all conversations). To turn off the plugin's, switch that tool off under "$t(settings:plugins.tab_tools)" on the plugin's detail page, or don't turn the plugin on for this conversation.

approval.title: Approval
approval.preset: In workspace conversations, whether plugin tools and MCP tools ask depends only on the permission preset at the bottom left of the input box: "$t(input:workspace_permission.confirm_each)" asks every time; "$t(input:workspace_permission.balanced)" and "$t(input:workspace_permission.full_access)" don't ask. If you change the preset mid-conversation, the next call uses the new one.
approval.always_allow: On an approval card you can choose "$t(message:tool_part.always_allow)": that tool stops asking in this conversation, and asking resumes after the app restarts.
approval.mcp_switch: The "$t(settings:mcp.server.needs_approval)" switch on MCP tools only applies in chat mode.
approval.sub_tasks: When a plugin runs a sub-task inside the current conversation, file access and commands in the sub-task are judged by the preset too. These calls have no approval card, so any that need your confirmation are refused.
approval.hook: Some plugins show their own prompt before a tool call. Such prompts aren't shown; that interception is dropped and approval is left to the app. A plugin that refuses without a prompt still takes effect, and the tool card says "Blocked by plugin …". To stop a plugin from intercepting, switch off "$t(settings:plugins.hook_tool_call)" under "$t(settings:plugins.tab_overview)" → "$t(settings:common.advanced)" on its detail page.

data.title: Plugin data
data.home: Plugins that store settings the way pi expects keep them under engines/pi in the app's data folder. Many plugins also write to your home folder (for example ~/.pi-lens, ~/.context-mode). Uninstalling removes the plugin package and the MCP servers it registered. Data the plugin stored itself isn't cleaned up; delete it yourself if needed.
data.backup: Backups between desktop installs include the plugin list but not the packages or the data plugins store themselves. After restoring on another computer, reinstall them on the plugins page. Backups for the mobile app don't include plugins.

engine.title: The engine process and restart notices
engine.process: Plugins and workspace conversations run in a separate engine process. It starts when you open a workspace conversation, exits after 15 minutes idle, and starts again when needed.
engine.unresponsive: "$t(page:conversations.engine_status.unresponsive)": the engine process hasn't answered for 5 seconds. This is common the first time a batch of plugins loads, or when searching a very large folder. You can wait; clicking stop ends it at once and starts a new process. If it still hasn't answered after 60 seconds, it is ended and restarted automatically.
engine.crashed: Notices like "$t(settings:app_errors.codes.engine_host_crashed)": when the engine process crashes or is force-stopped, a new one starts right away. If a reply was in progress, it ends as failed and queued messages pause; you can regenerate.
engine.gave_up: "…exited unexpectedly 3 times in a short period, so it will not be restarted": after 3 failures within 5 minutes the app stops restarting it. The notice lists the plugins that are on, and one of them is the likely cause. Disable them and regenerate; changing plugins or regenerating makes the app try again.
engine.where: Restart notices, including the one about no longer restarting, are recorded under "$t(settings:logs.filter_errors)" in "Settings → $t(settings:nav.stats) → $t(settings:subnav.stats.logs)".
